_search_meta.note: 1167017 (EB1B) and 1176775 are not clean multi-FTA1 timelines; 1179148/1177261 are 1-2 FTA1 (already studied).

patterns: 3+ FTA1 is a REAL, recurring phenomenon (not a glitch) — officer/supervisor repeatedly pulling the file.
FTA1 clusters often map to milestones: post-bio, pre-interview, interview-day, or supervisor-review passes. Repeat FTA1s 1-2 days apart (Justinllc 2nd+3rd, Theo 2nd+3rd) are common.
Outcome split: when PD IS current, 3-4 FTA1 resolved to APPROVAL in both clean cases (Justinllc, ddd1yy2) — one via RFE-then-approve (12d), one via silent->24h-approve (21d after last FTA1).

An RFE frequently fires right after the last FTA1 (Justinllc next-day, giacintayao). The RFEs seen were trivial (birth certificate already provided). RFE is part of the active-adjudication push, not a rejection signal.
When PD is NOT current (EB3 1174814), repeat FTA1 = officer picks up, can't approve, shelves it -> stays pending. This does NOT apply to Theo (PD current).
Terminal signal across approved cases: a SILENT UPDATE followed by approval within ~24h. Watch for that, not for the FTA1s themselves.
implication_for_theo: Theo's PD is current, interview waived, concurrent EB2 — matches the two APPROVED profiles (Justinllc, ddd1yy2) far more than the PENDING EB3 (PD-not-current) or the derivative giacintayao.
The 2nd+3rd FTA1 clustered 1 day apart mirrors Justinllc's 2nd+3rd (2 days). In his case that cluster preceded RFE-then-approval by ~12 days.

Realistic forward read: a 3rd FTA1 with current PD points toward terminal adjudication. Expect EITHER a silent-update->24h-approval OR a (likely trivial) RFE then approval. Both resolved within ~2-3 weeks of the last FTA1 in the approved cases.

This RAISES confidence that Theo is in the approval-imminent regime rather than the shelved/stuck regime, while keeping the RFE branch live (it appeared in 2 of 3 non-EB3 cases). Interview branch is weaker for Theo (waived) than ddd1yy2.
